candidates.name: Legionnaires' disease
support_spans: Positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine
febrile (Tmax 39.3°C [102.8 °F])
hypoxic with SpO₂ of 88% on room air
Right-sided lung infiltrates
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including a positive urine antigen test for Legionella pneumophila, are consistent with Legionnaires' disease.

candidates.name: Acute coronary syndrome
support_spans: high-sensitivity troponin: 102 μg/L (normal: <78 μg/L)
N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide: 1098 ng/L (normal: 0–900 ng/L)

ECG findings: Sinus tachycardia with old incomplete right bundle branch block, new left posterior fascicular block, multifocal PVCs, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, fascicular ventricular tachycardia
contradict_spans: Coronary angiography: Stable findings, no significant changes from previous
candidates.why: The patient's elevated troponin and BNP levels, as well as ECG changes, suggest acute coronary syndrome, but the stable coronary angiography findings contradict this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Myocarditis
support_spans: moderate subendocardial LGE in multiple segments
Subepicardial LGE in apical inferior wall and papillary muscles
FDG uptake in posteromedial papillary muscle and anterolateral wall
candidates.why: The patient's cardiac MRI and 18F-FDG-PET/CT findings, including late gadolinium enhancement and FDG uptake, are consistent with myocarditis.
